title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy
main_claim: There is a fixed j with the language of true sentences ∃x∈R^r ∀y∈R^s Φ(x,y) (polynomials given by arithmetic circuits) in C_j of the counting hierarchy; for ETR in particular, ETR ∈ C_26 (Theorem A.1).
coverage:
I read every section (2–6 and Appendix A) and checked each step by hand.
- Sec 2: the counting and product lemmas (levels of the discrete-log route); the coefficient-extraction cutoff p>d+1; substitution and derivative norm bounds; CRT sign recovery (count of primes ≥Z^3/5, Π≥2^{3Z}, k0≤Yb_Y+1, flagging window versus 2^-10 error).
- Sec 3: monomial basis via the Laurent functional; the Scheja–Storch trace proof (the (x')^τ coefficient of the Bezoutian is 1; reproducing identity); the eigenline lemma; truncation degrees in the char-coeff proposition and the exp/log trace formula mod p (p>D, D^2<p-1); determinant size bounds.
- Sec 4: root-value lower bound via the integral companion algebra; Thom separation; fingerprint prime μ>d^3 exists and γ avoids <d^3 bad values; rational sign approximant (the factor identity 2^{max(0,k)}=2^{max(0,-k)}2^k, error 2·3^{-2s}); the ±1/2 dichotomy for L_a, including b0=0.
- Sec 5: separated critical values at u=0 (2sin(π/ℓ)≥4/ℓ, geometric domination); the Sylvester-type Δ and its injectivity at u=0; root bounds giving R and U; the limit argument giving A_a(μ)=0; the IVT no-crossing argument; the sign determinant with the e-shift (real factors ≤-D or ≥2D, at most one e is bad per nonreal root).
- Sec 6: the quartic gadget for both atom types; the growth test with substitution u=v^{D+1}; E_D≡1; local constancy on degree pieces; the closed lift Z_d; the compact neighbourhood K with c* interior, so minimizers are critical; leading w-coefficient vanishing; soundness and completeness of the two existential tests.
- Appendix: sparse selection (⌈log2 5^n⌉≤3n); test-value bounds; Ψ thresholds (≤-1+1/(16T) when matching, ≥33/16 otherwise); |X| bound; level table 8→9→13→21→24→25→C26. The table is conservative: the actual counts are lower, e.g. a+8 could be max(a+3,4)+2.
sibling_notes: No sibling entries were in family 141 when I checked. The tools that other papers could reuse are the controlled-family closure rules, the multiplication-determinant rule over arbitrary coefficient rings, short root labels and the CRT sign test.
